html:
Verified execution cache

The execution cache stores reusable execution knowledge under explicit identity and safety constraints. Its runtime integration can focus the model's tool projection or reuse a verified procedure. It does not turn a cached response into fresh proof about mutable external state.

The running Controller owns cache records in indexed RAM through memory_store.py, with checkpoint durability. store.py selects that owner or standalone compatibility SQLite. Exact-prompt aliases share recipes while retaining independent output intent and pins; the learned LRU bound does not count pinned recipes.

identity.py and context.py bind current prompt/target/resource identity; extraction.py and safety.py validate receipt dependencies, schemas and effects. runtime.py, focus.py and direct.py integrate fresh execution with the native loop. The narrow direct path can save one model decision for an eligible single read. After verified reads finish, the ordinary authorized tools remain available for remaining work and completion still requires current evidence.

The management API under /api/agent/fast-cache inspects and pins receipt-backed steps or exact prompts without executing them. It does not grant permission for future reuse. Current literal handling preserves admitted argument values: the compatibility secret_check helper rejects lossy [redacted] markers only and does not scan credential values. See the authoritative guide below for these boundaries, management endpoints and recovery behavior.

A warm run still needs appropriate current execution evidence and completion validation. Discovery/capability policy and Agent Checks can affect eligibility and focus; a cache hit is not an authorization override. Review the current cache architecture guide for detailed source-backed constraints, and keep its historical acceptance measurements separate from promises about current performance.

Prompt pins and Settings

An eligible completed prompt shows a + control beside the user message. Select it to retain that exact prompt and its verified read plan; ✓ indicates a pin. The backend decides eligibility from the retained execution. A missing control can mean the plan is ineligible, still being captured, or unavailable to inspect. The browser does not infer eligibility from a successful-looking answer.

Open Settings → Fast Cache to inspect the retained prompt, read commands, working directory, Gateway, hit count and last-use observation. Pinned prompts, Learned and All filter the loaded list. Refresh requests another snapshot. Remove deletes the selected prompt association, or the underlying recipe for an unassigned recipe entry. Clear learned removes unpinned learned recipes while preserving pins. Removing a cache entry does not erase the original execution's receipts or undo its effects.

fast_cache.js implements both controls. The conversation owner attaches them to visible ordinary prompt rows, refreshes them when work completes and disposes their listeners/timers when a turn is removed. Historical turns inspect their durable request on attachment. Compact or continuation rows do not receive this prompt-extra control through that caller.

sequenceDiagram participant Turn as Conversation turn participant UI as Prompt pin control participant API as Fast Cache routes participant Proof as Management and retained proof participant Tabs as Participating tabs Turn->>UI: Attach history or refresh after completion UI->>UI: Wait for priority reads and advance generation UI->>API: GET prompt eligibility by request ID API->>Proof: Revalidate captured plan and source identity Proof-->>UI: Eligible/pinned projection or bounded reason alt Current ineligible response and fewer than three retries UI->>UI: Remove old control and retry after 400/800/1200 ms else Eligible and row/generation still current UI->>UI: Show unpinned or pinned control opt User selects unpinned control UI->>API: POST pin with request_id only API->>Proof: Revalidate again and retain exact prompt alt Acknowledged UI->>Tabs: Local event and BroadcastChannel invalidation Tabs->>API: Reread current retention state else Rejected UI->>UI: Restore action and show error label end end else Ineligible after the final retry UI->>UI: Keep the control absent else Request fails or row/response is obsolete UI->>UI: Remove failed current control or ignore obsolete response end

Each eligibility read waits for SMTOReadPriority.ready, then receives a local generation number. A later refresh or disposal invalidates an outstanding response; disconnected rows cannot accept it. An ineligible response permits three delayed rechecks because terminal trace delivery can precede capture. A request failure removes the current control without starting that retry sequence. These checks govern presentation, not server authority.

Pinning sends only request_id. The route rejects extra body fields, and management rebuilds and revalidates the retained plan before pinning. An earlier eligibility response is not a reservation: changed proof can make the subsequent mutation fail. Management does not execute the procedure or make a model call. Later reuse still follows the current execution constraints described in the cache architecture guide.

flowchart TD Mount[Mount Settings or select Refresh] --> Read[GET retained prompt/recipe entries] Local[Successful local pin, remove or clear] --> Hint[fast-cache-changed event] Local --> Channel[Same-origin BroadcastChannel hint] Channel --> Other[Other participating pages emit local hint] Other --> Hint Hint --> Read Hint --> Prompt[Refresh connected prompt controls] Read --> Success{Read succeeded?} Success -->|Yes| Snapshot[Replace local entries and counts] Snapshot --> Filter[Pinned / Learned / All filter] Filter --> Rows[Render text, read plan and availability] Success -->|No| Error[Keep prior rows and show request error] Rows --> Remove[Remove alias or unassigned recipe] Remove --> Mutation[Submit identity-based DELETE] Clear[Clear learned entries] --> Mutation Mutation --> Ack{Acknowledged?} Ack -->|Yes| Local Ack -->|No| Failure[Keep rows, show error and re-enable action]

Successful mutations notify the current page and participating same-origin tabs. They carry an invalidation hint; each listener requests its own authoritative view. If BroadcastChannel is unavailable, the current page still refreshes. This module does not subscribe to the general UI update stream or poll for independently learned entries. Mounting Settings and selecting Refresh are explicit read opportunities.

Settings retains its previous rows on a failed read. Its overlapping loads have no generation check, so the last response to finish supplies the visible list. Prompt controls have the stronger generation/connection checks described above. The filter works on the last loaded snapshot and does not request a different server result. Display text uses textContent; a missing retained display prompt remains an unassigned/hash label rather than being reconstructed from conversation history.

Verification boundaries

The browser scenarios describe prompt pinning, cross-tab removal, delayed capture, mutation failure and historical turns. Selected backend scenarios exercise identity-only bodies, changed receipts, independent retention and fresh execution. Their current shared fixture fails before these assertions with KeyError: 'data'; the same selected cases fail on the unchanged November 4 baseline. They are retained regression intentions, not passing browser evidence. The documentation refresh checks JavaScript syntax and exact executable AST/token preservation separately. See the refresh status for the recorded validation scope and remaining findings.
